script.text:
Lightning crackles night, sand stings shore, Dagobah Beach burns, my Hero Notebook trembles, One‑For‑All whispers, 85% power humming, while doubts flicker like

Morning rain smells metallic, I grind kettles, habit stacks like bricks, each rep echoing, stamina builds daily, fear recedes slowly, focus sharpens

When market roars, I picture collapse, breathe cold air, anchor offers sharply, label rivals’ anxiety, then strike relentless, no mercy ever, profit

Sometimes Sarah’s grin wavers,  
my confidence trembles,  
yet I remember,

director.hook: Deku didn't become the strongest hero overnight. He stacked 1% micro-wins while everyone else slept.
director.angle: Translate the concept of 'Atomic Habits' into Izuku Midoriya's brutal training journey—showing how pulling trash on the beach compounded into wielding One For All.
images: 15-year-old Izuku weeping on Dagobah Beach surrounded by mountains of rust and iron.
Fast-cut montage: Deku scribbling furiously in Hero Analysis Vol. 13 at 2 AM, clock ticking.
High-energy transformation cut: Green lightning explodes as Full Cowl jumps from 5% to 20% to 100%.
director.style: Dark motivational anime edit, fast text-on-screen overlay, high-contrast green aura effects, heavy bass/phonk build-up into cinematic orchestral drop.
director.title_suggestion: The 1% Rule That Made Deku Unstoppable ⚡ | Anime Motivation
director.reasoning: The core topic (Compound Habits) is a perfect fit for the Izuku Midoriya niche, but the draft script is totally wrong for the audience. The text reads like poetic corporate prose ('espresso', 'market volatility', 'Raj', 'jasmine'). Anime short-form viewers will swipe away instantly. Midoriya represents raw effort, grit, notebooks, and physical sacrifice—the script must reflect that energy.
director.changes_if_revise:
1. Throw out the corporate/poetic script entirely.
2. Write a fast-paced, high-intensity voiceover using Deku-specific lore (Dagobah Beach, Hero Notebooks, One For All percentages).
3. Keep sentences short (3-6 words per line) so it hits hard on beat drops.
4. Shift from reflective monologue to aggressive, call-to-action motivational speech.
